states.description: Mean arterial pressure in millimeters of mercury
Normalized autonomic vasomotor drive, with zero representing minimal drive and one representing maximal drive

scenario_text: Model short-term arterial pressure regulation after the circulation begins away from its resting operating point. Mean arterial pressure changes through the imbalance between cardiac delivery and peripheral runoff, while autonomic vasomotor drive is adjusted by pressure-sensitive feedback and relaxes toward a pressure-dependent command level. Posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and circulating hormone levels remain fixed background conditions during the observation window. The scientific target is the instantaneous rate of change of mean arterial pressure along the coupled pressure-control trajectory.

derivation_notes: The resistance pathway is re-derived by replacing the linear autonomic recruitment law with a saturating monotone effector law, peripheral_resistance_baseline + peripheral_resistance_gain*(vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-S/vascular_saturation_scale))). The factor vascular_saturation_scale preserves the local small-S slope so the parent is recovered when the saturation scale is large relative to the sampled S range.
change_summary: The vascular effect of autonomic drive is no longer assumed linear across the full drive range; instead it saturates because arteriolar smooth-muscle recruitment has finite capacity. This changes the scored mapping dP_dt(P,S) directly by steepening low-to-moderate resistance recruitment while flattening the marginal pressor effect at high S.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Peripheral resistance responds linearly to autonomic drive across the full normalized drive range.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite vascular smooth-muscle and arteriolar receptor recruitment causes diminishing additional peripheral resistance at high autonomic drive.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit vascular_saturation_scale >> S over the observed trajectory, because vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-S/vascular_saturation_scale)) approaches S.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed P, autonomic drive S changes cardiac delivery and peripheral resistance with constant linear gains, so the target mapping dP_dt versus S has one fixed curvature set only by the reciprocal runoff term.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the linear vascular actuation assumption so that the resistance effect of S saturates at high drive, making the target mapping dP_dt versus S bend more strongly at low to moderate S and flatten at high S.
response_change.observable_effect: During trajectories that transiently span low and high autonomic drive, pressure recovery becomes initially more sensitive to S but shows diminishing additional pressor effect near maximal drive, compared with the parent's continued near-linear increase in vasomotor effect.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the trajectory visits a broad enough S range, especially moderate-to-high vasomotor drive where further resistance recruitment should taper rather than increase indefinitely; P must remain positive and within the sampled transient recovery range.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, low-to-moderate S still resembles the parent law, but holdout segments reaching stronger sympathetic activation reveal diminishing incremental pressure support from additional S that one shared linear-gain parent cannot match simultaneously with the low-S slope.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the saturation scale is large enough that the saturating resistance law is effectively linear over the observed S range.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Saturating vasoconstrictor recruitment in peripheral resistance control
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite vascular smooth-muscle and arteriolar receptor recruitment causes diminishing additional peripheral resistance at high autonomic drive even while neural drive S continues to increase.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the functional form of the runoff denominator, introducing a new saturation scale that alters the S-dependent curvature of the scored target mapping rather than merely rescaling one gain.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Peripheral resistance recruitment by autonomic drive is linear with one constant gain over the whole normalized drive range.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Peripheral resistance recruitment by autonomic drive is monotone but saturating, with a distinct saturation scale for high-drive tapering.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when vascular_saturation_scale is sufficiently large compared with the observed S range so that vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-S/vascular_saturation_scale)) is approximately S.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Along transient recoveries from the prescribed initial condition, segments that reach stronger hypotensive activation show a steeper early change of dP_dt with S but reduced incremental runoff suppression at high S because the resistance contribution flattens; one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the low-S sensitivity and the high-S tapering over those same observed trajectories.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters still forces peripheral resistance to depend linearly on S, so the parent preserves one shared marginal resistance gain across low and high autonomic drive. That single-gain structure cannot simultaneously reproduce the child's near-parent low-S behavior and the reduced high-S incremental pressor support seen when S traverses a broad range during the same trajectory.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes autonomic vasomotor drive recruits peripheral resistance with a constant gain across the full normalized drive range, omitting physiological saturation of vasoconstrictor effect.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite vascular smooth-muscle and arteriolar receptor recruitment causes diminishing additional peripheral resistance at high autonomic drive even while neural drive S continues to increase.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to keep the same states and feedback architecture but replace the linear S-to-resistance mapping with a saturating monotone form. The parent target relation from observed states to dP_dt is effectively governed by one shared vascular gain, so at fixed P it cannot express both a steep early vasoconstrictor effect and diminished marginal effect near high S. Varying condition: the coupled transient is observed from the prescribed initial condition while P and S evolve naturally, so different times along the trajectory sample different S levels; held fixed: posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, hormones, and the baroreflex command form. Observable contrast: under stronger hypotensive excursions that drive S toward its upper range, the child predicts flattening of the pressor benefit from further S increases, whereas the parent keeps adding resistance approximately linearly and therefore overstates late high-drive support if fitted to early low-drive behavior. This changes the scored target mapping dP_dt(P,S), not merely the auxiliary S trajectory, because the runoff denominator itself acquires different S-curvature. The effect is admissible whenever S reaches moderate to high values; if all data remain near a narrow low-S band, the refinement may be weakly identifiable, and in that restricted regime the parent is approximately recovered.

derivation_notes: The pressure balance is retained, but the resistance-recruitment branch no longer follows S instantaneously; instead a vascular effector state R relaxes toward the same saturating command with its own finite time constant. The initial condition R=vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-0.5/vascular_saturation_scale)) matches the parent's steady algebraic resistance command at the inherited initial S=0.5, avoiding an artificial startup mismatch while preserving a non-degenerate feedback branch thereafter.
change_summary: The single-phase autonomic assumption was relaxed only for the vascular branch by introducing a lagged resistance effector state. This creates a genuine phase shift in the target mapping because dP_dt can now differ at the same instantaneous P and S depending on the delayed vascular state R.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite arteriolar smooth-muscle activation and constrictor transduction delay peripheral resistance recruitment after changes in autonomic vasomotor drive.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Taking vascular_time_constant -> 0 forces R -> vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-S/vascular_saturation_scale)), recovering the parent pressure equation.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed P and S, the target dP_dt responds immediately to autonomic drive through both cardiac delivery and peripheral resistance, so the pressure trajectory has a single effective autonomic phase set only by S.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same pressure-balance structure but release the assumption that vascular resistance follows S instantaneously; instead, resistance recruitment relaxes toward the saturating command with its own finite vasomotor phase, so dP_dt depends on P, S, and a lagged vascular effector state.
response_change.observable_effect: After a pressure perturbation, early pressure recovery can show prompt cardiac support while runoff reduction develops later, creating a two-timescale pressure response that the parent cannot match with one shared autonomic phase.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when pressure is displaced enough that S moves appreciably away from its initial value over the observation window and vascular adjustment is not effectively instantaneous relative to autonomic_time_constant; especially during the first few vascular time constants after onset.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training windows with modest transients, the mechanism appears as a delayed runoff response relative to the rise or fall in S; in holdout conditions with larger or faster pressure excursions from the same initial conditions, the same lag extends into a clearer separation between early cardiac-driven and later resistance-driven pressure recovery.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the new vascular effector time constant to zero so the vascular state instantaneously equals the parent saturating function of S.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A finite vascular response lag cannot be represented by refitting existing static gains or the single S state, because the needed memory of past S is absent unless a separate dynamical vascular effector is introduced.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Delayed arteriolar resistance recruitment downstream of autonomic drive
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite arteriolar smooth-muscle activation and constrictor transduction delay peripheral resistance recruitment after changes in autonomic vasomotor drive.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient correction because the runoff term now depends on a separate internal memory state coupled to S, allowing different dP_dt values at the same instantaneous P and S during transients.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Cardiac delivery still follows S promptly, but vascular resistance recruitment evolves with its own finite relaxation dynamics toward the saturating autonomic command.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Taking vascular_time_constant -> 0 forces R = vascular_saturation_scale*(1 - exp(-S/vascular_saturation_scale)), which exactly recovers the parent target expression.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones fixed, vary the size or timing of the pressure displacement from the common initial conditions. In the parent, once P and S are observed, dP_dt is fixed because runoff changes immediately with S. In the child, for the same instantaneous P and S reached along different transient histories within the first few vascular time constants, dP_dt can differ because R lags behind the saturating resistance command. The visible contrast is weaker early runoff reduction but preserved prompt cardiac support after onset, followed later by stronger resistance-mediated pressure recovery.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both early weak resistance response and later stronger resistance recruitment across these conditions because the parent runoff term is an instantaneous function of only P and S. Refitting gains, saturation scale, or autonomic_time_constant can change overall slope or timing of S, but cannot create history dependence in dP_dt at fixed observed P and S without the added vascular memory state.

Here that gain is attenuated by an exponential afterload factor exp(-P/cardiac_afterload_pressure_scale), representing reduced conversion of autonomic drive into forward arterial inflow as mean arterial pressure rises.
change_summary: The cardiac autonomic contribution was refined from a fixed linear term to a pressure-dependent effective gain. This creates a direct P-by-S interaction in the target equation so identical increases in S have smaller effects on dP_dt at higher P.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Autonomic drive increases cardiac delivery with one pressure-independent gain despite changing arterial afterload.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Pressure-dependent cardiac afterload reduces the effective conversion of autonomic drive into arterial inflow at higher mean arterial pressure.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As cardiac_afterload_pressure_scale becomes much larger than the pressure range visited, exp(-P/cardiac_afterload_pressure_scale) approaches 1 and the parent law is recovered.

response_change.child_relation: Replace the fixed cardiac autonomic gain with a pressure-dependent effectiveness so the contribution of S to dP_dt weakens as P rises, creating a P-by-S interaction in the target mapping.
response_change.observable_effect: For the same increase in S, dP_dt rises more strongly at lower P than at higher P, beyond the runoff term alone.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, low-P recovery segments and higher-P segments can show different dP_dt sensitivity to the same S level; in holdout, the same mechanism extends this contrast to larger pressure excursions without changing background conditions.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the pressure dependence of cardiac autonomic effectiveness to zero, yielding a constant gain from S to cardiac delivery.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes autonomic drive increases cardiac delivery with one pressure-independent gain, omitting that elevated arterial pressure increases afterload and can blunt the pressure-generating benefit of sympathetic drive.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Pressure-dependent cardiac afterload reduces the effective conversion of autonomic drive into arterial inflow at higher mean arterial pressure.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-gain cardiac term rather than add an unrelated process. The parent target mapping is shortcut by a single_gain assumption: at fixed R, the partial effect of S on dP_dt is constant apart from division by arterial_compliance. Scientifically, higher arterial pressure raises ventricular afterload, so the same autonomic drive need not produce the same net forward delivery into the arterial compartment at high versus low pressure. Under the stated scenario, posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones stay fixed; the varied condition is the pressure level reached along the observed recovery trajectory, with S and P co-sampled by the solver and R retained as an existing state. The child therefore changes the target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory, by making the S-to-dP_dt slope depend on P. Observable contrast: compare segments with similar R and non-saturated S but different P; the child predicts weaker positive sensitivity of dP_dt to S at higher P than the parent can provide with one shared cardiac_delivery_gain. This is admissible for moderate pressure excursions where afterload effects are physiologically relevant and pressure remains nonnegative. Limitation: if observations remain in a very narrow pressure band or S is nearly saturated throughout, the contrast will be weak.

derivation_notes: The fixed baroreflex threshold is relaxed by introducing a slow resetting state B that tracks sustained pressure deviation and shifts the half-activation pressure seen by the S dynamics. The initial condition B=0 preserves the inherited baseline threshold at the start, so the new feedback branch is initially closed and only activates after continued pressure exposure.
change_summary: The pressure-sensitive feedback law is made history-dependent by allowing its effective setpoint to reset slowly toward recently experienced arterial pressure. This changes the scored P-to-dP_dt mapping under prolonged pressure excursions because identical current P can yield different autonomic drive after different exposure durations.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Slow baroreceptor and central reflex resetting shifts the effective pressure setpoint toward recently experienced arterial pressure, altering autonomic responsiveness during continued non-resting conditions.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Taking baroreflex_resetting_gain to zero or baroreflex_resetting_time_constant to infinity keeps B at zero so the effective threshold remains pressure_setpoint and the parent system is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The baroreflex command for S is a fixed logistic function of P alone, so the pressure at which autonomic drive is half-activated is constant and independent of recent pressure history.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the fixed pressure half-activation with a slowly adaptive effective setpoint driven by recent pressure exposure, so the instantaneous P-to-dP_dt mapping depends on both current pressure and the history state of baroreflex resetting.
response_change.observable_effect: After a sustained pressure elevation or depression, the same instantaneous pressure P produces a different autonomic drive and therefore a different dP_dt than it does early in the trajectory; recovery weakens after prolonged exposure because the feedback threshold has shifted toward the experienced pressure.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when pressure remains displaced from the nominal setpoint for a duration comparable to or longer than a plausible baroreflex resetting time, while P traverses a range of order baroreflex_pressure_scale so that threshold motion materially changes S.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early transients still resemble the parent because resetting is initially small; in longer or more prolonged deviations, holdout trajectories show that identical current P values reached after different exposure histories produce different dP_dt, extending the same threshold-shift mechanism rather than introducing a new regime.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the resetting time constant to infinity or the resetting gain to zero, which freezes the effective setpoint at pressure_setpoint.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A history-dependent moving baroreflex threshold cannot be represented with the existing Markov state set {P,S,R} without conflating instantaneous neural drive with slow reflex resetting; a separate state is needed to encode recent pressure exposure.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Short-term baroreflex resetting that shifts the effective half-activation pressure of autonomic drive
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Slow baroreceptor and central reflex resetting shifts the effective pressure setpoint toward recently experienced arterial pressure, altering autonomic responsiveness during continued non-resting conditions.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added resetting state creates competition between the baseline threshold and exposure-driven threshold motion in different pressure-history regions, so one static logistic curve is replaced by a moving threshold surface. This cannot be mimicked by a coefficient-only correction because the target mapping changes with exposure history even at the same current pressure.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective baroreflex threshold resets slowly toward recent pressure exposure, making feedback history-dependent during sustained perturbations.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Taking baroreflex_resetting_gain to zero or baroreflex_resetting_time_constant to infinity keeps B at zero so the effective threshold remains pressure_setpoint and the parent system is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Under the same fixed background conditions and same initial P,S,R, early in a pressure excursion the child nearly matches the parent, but after sustained elevation or depression the shifted threshold causes identical current P values to map to different S and therefore different dP_dt. The change is visible in the scored target because the P equation depends on S, and S now depends on both P and the resetting state B rather than on P alone.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can choose only one static pressure_setpoint and one static baroreflex_pressure_scale, so it cannot reproduce both early strong correction and later weakened correction for the same current P after different exposure durations. evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the pressure-sensitive feedback curve is time invariant, omitting short-term baroreflex resetting/accommodation during sustained pressure perturbations.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Slow baroreceptor and central reflex resetting shifts the effective pressure setpoint toward recently experienced arterial pressure, altering autonomic responsiveness during continued non-resting conditions.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping from observed states to dP_dt is effectively governed by a fixed baroreflex threshold: for fixed R and parameters, increasing P always suppresses S according to one unchanging logistic curve, so any two moments with the same current P and similar R are forced toward the same feedback-mediated inflow reduction. A realistic refinement is short-term baroreflex resetting, which changes that threshold after sustained pressure displacement. Under the admissible protocol, vary the duration of a pressure excursion generated from the given initial condition while holding posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormone background fixed as required. Early after the excursion begins, the child behaves close to the parent; later, the effective threshold has shifted toward the prevailing pressure, so at the same current P the child exhibits less restoring autonomic drive and therefore a different dP_dt. This is a genuine change in the scored target mapping, not only an auxiliary-state modification, because the pressure-to-dP_dt relation itself becomes history-dependent through the moving threshold. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both the early strong correction and the later weakened correction across these conditions, because changing pressure_setpoint or baroreflex_pressure_scale only selects one static logistic curve rather than a trajectory-dependent family of curves. The effect is strongest when the pressure deviation persists long enough for resetting to develop and when the deviation size is not negligible relative to baroreflex_pressure_scale; if observations are too short, the refinement may be weakly identifiable.

change_summary: I refined the baroreflex feedback law by making its pressure-sensitivity coefficient state dependent through the effective pressure error. assumption_audit.released_assumption: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation uses one symmetric logistic pressure scale above and below the effective setpoint.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Short-term arterial baroreflex signaling can have unequal gain on hypotensive and hypertensive sides because receptor saturation and central efferent recruitment are not perfectly symmetric around the operating point.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting baroreflex_asymmetry_gain = 0 restores the original symmetric logistic command law and exactly recovers the parent system.

response_change.parent_relation: The autonomic command driving S is a symmetric logistic function of the shifted pressure error P-(pressure_setpoint+B), so dP_dt inherits one fixed baroreflex sensitivity scale around a single midpoint.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the symmetric logistic pressure-command relation with an asymmetric pressure-response shape using the same states and parameters, so dP_dt changes more sharply on one side of the effective setpoint than the other while remaining monotone nonincreasing in pressure.
response_change.observable_effect: During comparable excursions below versus above the effective setpoint, pressure recovery and overshoot damping become unequal: one side shows steeper autonomic recruitment per mmHg than the other, which changes the local curvature of dP_dt versus pressure along the observed trajectory.

evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, asymmetric recovery is already visible in transients that traverse the effective setpoint neighborhood; in holdout, larger but still admissible deviations extend the same one-sided steepness difference, revealing curvature that a symmetric one-scale logistic cannot match with one shared parameter set.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: The child reduces to the parent in the symmetry-restoring limit where the modified pressure-command shape becomes the original logistic with one shared baroreflex_pressure_scale on both sides of the effective setpoint.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Short-term arterial baroreflex signaling can show unequal gain on hypotensive versus hypertensive sides because receptor firing saturation and central efferent recruitment are not perfectly symmetric around the operating point.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective logistic slope now depends on the evolving signed pressure error, so the same parameter set produces different local curvature above and below the reset setpoint rather than a uniform rescaling.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window, with a symmetric logistic shape around a single midpoint and one shared pressure scale.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The baroreflex remains smooth and monotone but its pressure sensitivity varies with signed effective pressure error, producing asymmetric steepness about the reset setpoint.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: The scored target expression keeps the same algebraic dependence on S and R, but along trajectories that sample both signs of P-(pressure_setpoint+B), the successor produces unequal dP_dt-versus-P curvature on the two sides because the S command law uses a state-dependent pressure scale. This is observable for deviations on the order of baroreflex_pressure_scale with posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones held fixed.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's single baroreflex_pressure_scale can match only one average steepness, not simultaneously the steeper hypotensive recruitment and flatter hypertensive suppression or vice versa across both sides of the effective setpoint with one shared parameter set. The change is therefore not absorbable by global coefficient retuning when both sides of the command curve are observed.

Holding posture, volume status, metabolic demand, and hormones fixed as required, vary only the trajectory's pressure excursion relative to the current effective setpoint. Then compare transients that spend time moderately below versus moderately above that setpoint. In the parent, the slope of the command curve as a function of P is determined by one shared scale, so the shape of dP_dt versus P near low-pressure recovery and high-pressure suppression remains constrained to be symmetric up to the downstream inflow/runoff nonlinearities already present. But across both sides with one shared parameter set, the parent cannot simultaneously reproduce unequal low-pressure recovery steepness and high-pressure damping curvature if the underlying command law remains symmetric.
